title: Farm Stay Holidays Booming in the UK
paragraphs: Waking up to the sound of sheep, collecting fresh eggs for breakfast and spending the evening by a wood-burning stove: for a growing number of British holidaymakers, this is the ideal way to spend a break. Farm stays, or "farmcations," as they are sometimes called, are becoming one of the fastest-growing travel trends in the UK.

According to data released in July 2026 by the accommodation company Airbnb, bookings of farm stays by UK guests for the summer of 2026 rose by 14% compared with the same period in 2025. The increase was even sharper among younger travelers, with bookings by Gen Z guests, aged 18 to 28, rising by 41%. At the same time, searches by UK guests for British destinations rose by more than 11%.

Some areas saw particularly dramatic growth. In Ceredigion, on the west coast of Wales, farm stay bookings tripled, rising by 200%. Bookings also doubled in Powys, Wales, and increased by 78% in the Highland region of Scotland and by 71% in Eden, in Cumbria.

The most popular properties on Airbnb's wish lists included a cabin on a working sheep farm in Shropshire, a cottage in the Scottish Highlands with a wood-fired hot tub and a stone barn dating from 1640 on a working farm. In addition to accommodation, guests are booking activities such as guided tours, food experiences and wellness sessions, while nature and outdoor activities are among Airbnb's most popular experience categories for UK guests.

Lisa Marçais of Airbnb said that the trend "shows it's the great British countryside that's capturing people's attention." The growing interest has been linked to lifestyle trends such as "cottagecore" and slow living, as well as to the popular TV series Clarkson's Farm, which follows the TV presenter Jeremy Clarkson as he runs a farm.

For farmers, the trend can also provide a valuable additional source of income. However, it should be noted that the figures come from a single company's booking data, and there are no independent national statistics on the size of the market.
